name: Chinvat Bridge
note: The Cinvat (Chinvat) Bridge, the 'bridge of the separator/accountant' which every soul must cross after death; attested in the Gathas (Y. 46.10, 51.13) and the Vendidad (19), where Rashnu, Mithra and Sraosha judge and the Daena meets the soul. Widens for the righteous, narrows to a blade for the wicked.

name: Garothman (House of Song)
note: Garothman / Garodman, the 'House of Song' (Avestan Garo-demana), the highest paradise and abode of Ahura Mazda and the blessed (the 'Best Existence', vahishta ahu). Attested in the Avesta and elaborated in the Bundahishn and Menog-i Khrad.

name: Drujo Demana (House of Lies)
note: Drujo Demana, the 'House of the Lie' (Avestan druj-demana), the Zoroastrian hell and abode of Angra Mainyu and the damned (the 'Worst Existence'). Antithesis of the House of Song; attested in the Gathas (Y. 46.11, 49.11) and Pahlavi eschatology.

name: Hamistagan
note: Hamistagan (Pahlavi hammistagan), the neutral 'place of the mixed', an intermediate state for souls whose good and evil deeds are exactly balanced; they remain there, untormented but joyless, until the final renovation (Frashokereti). Attested in the Bundahishn and Menog-i Khrad.

name: Irkalla (Kur)
note: Irkalla (Sumerian Kur, the 'land of no return'), the Mesopotamian underworld ruled by Ereshkigal (and Nergal), a dark dust-filled realm where the dead eat clay. Attested in the Descent of Ishtar and the Descent of Inanna. NOTE: distinct from the being Apsu (ENT_MES_APSU); this is the place.

name: Ganzir
note: Ganzir, the gate / threshold (the 'face') of the netherworld Irkalla/Kur, sometimes used as a name for the underworld's entrance through which the dead pass the seven gates. Attested in the Descent of Inanna/Ishtar tradition.

name: Dilmun
note: Dilmun, the 'pure, clean, bright' land where there is no death or sickness, watered with fresh water by Enki; the Sumerian paradise (and a real geographical region, Bahrain). Attested in the myth Enki and Ninhursag.

name: The Seven Heavens (Vilon, Raqia, Shehaqim, Zebul, Maon, Makhon, Araboth)
note: The seven heavens of rabbinic/Merkavah cosmology, named in b. Hagigah 12b: Vilon, Raqia, Shehaqim, Zebul, Maon, Makhon, and Araboth (the highest, housing the Throne of Glory). Distinct from the seven firmaments of Sefer ha-Razim.

name: The Seven Hekhalot (Heavenly Palaces)
note: The seven hekhalot ('palaces'/'halls') nested within the highest heaven (Araboth), each guarded by angelic gatekeepers, through which the yored merkavah ('descender to the chariot') ascends to the Throne. Attested in Hekhalot Rabbati.
